snippet.title: My Perfect Thai Farm is a LIE
snippet.description:
Is our Permaculture farm in Thailand a complete waste of money? 🤔 

After leaving the UK for a new life, I was determined to build a "perfect" farm in rural Thailand, following the permaculture principles I'd read so much about. But the reality of running a farm has been a very expensive and uncomfortable lesson.

In this video, I'm sharing the full story. We'll explore the unexpected costs—from the mystery of which cow wrecked my car, to the makeshift repair of a fallen electric pylon during a storm. I’ll also give you a tour of our beautiful (and expensive) duck and turkey coop, a perfect symbol of how my idealism led to overspending.

But the biggest "uncomfortable truth" is this: I was wrong. My initial approach to Permaculture, while beautiful, is not a profitable or scalable model for the local farmers who depend on this land for their livelihood. 

This project was becoming a money pit, disconnected from the financial realities of farming.

This isn't just a story of failure, though. It’s a story of a pivot. I'll introduce the new, scientific approach we're taking, inspired by Dr. Elaine Ingham's Soil Food Web composting methods (https://www.soilfoodweb.com/), to create a system that is truly sustainable—both for the environment AND the bank account. Join me on this journey as we try to turn our beautiful mistake into a genuine success.

🌍 READ MORE & GET IN TOUCH!

For more detailed blog posts about our farm life, permaculture critiques, and life in Thailand, or to contact me directly, please visit my website:

► https://farang-farm.com/

This is the real story of our life in rural Isaan, a journey from a romanticized dream to a pragmatic, new beginning.

snippet.title: ⚠️ If You’re 60+… The Philippines Says You’re Not Finished
snippet.description:
What happens to men when they reach their later years in the West?

For many men, life begins to shrink.

The kids grow up and move away.
Friend circles get smaller.
Divorce rates increase.
And suddenly many men find themselves living alone with fewer social connections than they had earlier in life.

In the United States and other Western countries, loneliness among men has become a growing issue. Studies show millions of adults experience isolation, and many older adults now live alone.

But some men are discovering that the story doesn’t have to end that way.

In countries like the Philippines, the social dynamics are different. Older men are often still valued for the stability, experience, and resources they bring to relationships and family life.

In this video we talk about:

• why loneliness among men in the West is increasing
• why some Western men move to Southeast Asia
• the cultural differences between Western and Filipino relationship dynamics
• the provider role in traditional societies
• common mistakes men make when coming to the Philippines
• real examples of men building new lives abroad

This is not about fantasy.

It’s about understanding different cultures, different relationship dynamics, and the choices men have when deciding how they want to live the final chapters of their life.

If you’re interested in expat life, the Philippines, Southeast Asia, relationships, or cultural differences between the West and Asia, this video will give you a perspective that isn’t often talked about openly.

snippet.title: The Uncomfortable Truth About Thailand in 2026 🇹🇭
snippet.description:
Thailand is still one of the most beautiful countries in the world.

The beaches. The food. The nightlife. The culture. The lifestyle.

There’s a reason millions of people continue to visit Thailand every year.

But after years of living in Thailand and watching the country evolve, I started noticing something many foreigners, expats, retirees, and long-term visitors are beginning to feel.

The relationship is changing.

From increased scrutiny at immigration to changing tourism priorities, tighter enforcement, proof-of-funds requirements, growing tensions between locals and foreigners, and the push toward higher-spending visitors, Thailand today feels very different from the Thailand many people fell in love with years ago.

This video isn’t about hating Thailand.

It’s about understanding Thailand.

Because sometimes the truth hits harder than the fantasy.

👇 Let me know in the comments:

Has Thailand changed, or are foreigners just refusing to adapt?

snippet.description:
I’ll never marry a Filipina — not because of the woman, but because of what really happens to a Western man’s freedom once he signs that paper.

A lot of guys leave the US, UK, Canada, Australia thinking marriage in the Philippines will finally give them peace, loyalty, and a fresh start.
What they don’t see is the system behind the ring:
 • legal traps in every country
 • financial responsibility they never agreed to
 • family obligations and emergencies that become their problem
 • losing leverage, options, and control over their own life

This video isn’t anti-Filipina.
It’s pro-freedom and pro-reality for Western men.

In 7 minutes I break down:
 • why Western men get crushed by systems in the West and abroad
 • how marriage turns you from a free man into a lifeline
 • how properties, families, and cultural responsibilities can lock you in
 • why staying unmarried can protect your peace, your money, and your future

snippet.title: Exit 4 BTS Phloen Chit, Siam Pharmacy Bangkok
snippet.description:
Siam Pharmacy – Popular and well-reviewed pharmacy in Phloen Chit (Bangkok) where expats often check medication availability and may be able to purchase common drugs.
Filling prescriptions:
Once you have a Thai doctor’s prescription (ใบสั่งยา / bai-sang-ya), you can take it to most pharmacies to have it filled. This often includes both private and independent pharmacies.

Over-the-counter availability:
Many common medications (painkillers, antihistamines, cough medicine) are available without a formal prescription in Thai pharmacies. Some antibiotics and other drugs that require a prescription elsewhere may still be available over the counter depending on the pharmacy.
